reference: No GNU CLI implements this Bash builtin. Runnable expected values are fixed independently from Python's UTF-8 replacement decoder, str.lower/upper/title/casefold and unicodedata.normalize, plus UAX #29 grapheme rules and Unicode width properties for the selected examples. Bash type/help expectations follow the Bash builtin metadata contract. These are contract checks, not GNU parity; no expected value comes from the candidate.
coverage: Bash builtin type and registered help metadata
Grapheme, codepoint, byte and display-width length modes on mixed UTF-8
Grapheme, codepoint, byte and display-width slicing boundaries
Unicode lower, upper and title mappings, including expansion and final sigma
Canonical and compatibility normalization, including algorithmic Hangul
Full casefold output and cmp equality, inequality and normalization options
-V output binding and preservation of surrounding spaces
Malformed UTF-8 replacement and invalid mode/form status handling
Empty transformations and slice endpoint boundaries.
exclusions: No same-name GNU/POSIX command exists, so runnable operation cases use independent contract values rather than fabricated parity comparisons.
Full Unicode 17 normalization/case-mapping coverage and exhaustive UAX #29 conformance need pinned reference data; an exhaustive grapheme case is deferred.
Locale/libc-dependent display width modes are not asserted; the runnable width case names the deterministic wcwidth table backend.
Bash arguments cannot contain NUL bytes, so embedded-NUL input is outside this interface suite.

cases.purpose: Confirm utf8 is registered as a Bash builtin and help has a nonempty topic, using only Bash metadata builtins.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t utf8)
doc=$(help utf8)
[[ $kind == builtin && -n $doc ]]
printf '%s\n%s\n' "$kind" help-registered

cases.purpose: Check grapheme, codepoint, byte and wcwidth counts across ASCII, accented text, a regional-indicator flag, a combining sequence and a ZWJ emoji.
cases.script:
text='Aé🇺🇳á👩‍💻'
utf8 length "$text"
utf8 length "$text" -T codepoint
utf8 length "$text" -T byte
utf8 length "$text" -T width -L wcwidth

cases.purpose: Verify half-open slice indexes in grapheme and codepoint modes, including selecting only a combining mark, plus byte slicing on ASCII.
cases.script:
text='Aé😀Z'
utf8 slice "$text" 1 2
utf8 slice "$text" 1 2 -T codepoint
utf8 slice "$text" 2 3 -T codepoint
utf8 slice abcdef 1 4 -T byte

cases.purpose: Check display-width slice bounds around a two-cell CJK scalar with the explicit wcwidth table backend.
Cover Unicode lower, upper and title operations with Greek final sigma, sharp-s expansion and mixed-case words.
cases.script:
utf8 lower 'ΟΣ'
utf8 upper 'straße'
utf8 title 'hELLo wORLD'

cases.purpose: Check NFC/NFD canonical composition and decomposition, NFKC/NFKD compatibility mappings, and Hangul algorithmic normalization.
cases.script:
utf8 normalize NFC 'Å'
utf8 normalize NFD 'Å'
utf8 normalize NFKC 'ﬁ'
utf8 normalize NFKD '²'
utf8 normalize NFD '각'
utf8 normalize NFC '각'

cases.purpose: Check full casefold expansion, case-insensitive cmp, normalized cmp, and the non-equal return status.
cases.script:
utf8 casefold 'Straße Σς'
if utf8 cmp 'Straße' 'STRASSE' -i; then printf 'case-insensitive-equal
'; else exit 41; fi
if utf8 cmp 'Å' 'Å' -N NFC; then printf 'nfc-equal
'; else exit 42; fi
if utf8 cmp cat dog; then printf 'unexpected-equal
'; else rc=$?; printf 'different-status:%s
' "$rc"; fi

cases.purpose: Verify -V binds transformed text without emitting command output and preserves leading/trailing spaces.
cases.script:
utf8 upper '  Straße  ' -V mapped
[[ $mapped == '  STRASSE  ' ]]
utf8 casefold 'Straße' -V folded
[[ $folded == strasse ]]
printf 'mapped=<%s>\nfolded=<%s>\n' "$mapped" "$folded"

cases.purpose: Check the documented Python-compatible replacement policy for a truncated multibyte sequence in codepoint counting and normalization.
cases.script:
bad=$'\xe2\x82'
utf8 length "$bad" -T codepoint
utf8 normalize NFC "$bad"

cases.purpose: Check usage failure status and diagnostics for an unsupported normalization form and length mode.
cases.script:
if utf8 normalize BAD 'x'; then nrc=0; else nrc=$?; fi
if utf8 length x -T words; then lrc=0; else lrc=$?; fi
printf 'normalize-status=%d\nlength-status=%d\n' "$nrc" "$lrc"

cases.purpose: Exercise the complete Unicode grapheme boundary corpus through length and slice operations.
cases.reason: The normative reference group already executes the complete expressible corpus with the pinned Unicode 17 GraphemeBreakTest and an independent oracle (the file's own break marks); no utf8 grapheme assertion failed. The only remainder is the NUL subset, which the interface cannot express.

cases.purpose: Empty strings have zero length; empty transformations and an empty in-range half-open slice produce only their newline delimiter.
cases.script:
utf8 length ''
utf8 length '' -T byte
utf8 normalize NFC ''
utf8 casefold ''
utf8 slice abc 1 1

cases.purpose: Half-open substring bounds past the end of an ASCII string yield an empty string, independently matching Python string slicing. Compare grapheme/codepoint/byte modes without Unicode boundary ambiguity.
cases.script:
for mode in grapheme codepoint byte; do
 utf8 slice abc 9 12 -T "$mode"
done

cases.purpose: Half-open valid Unicode grapheme/codepoint slices clamp both bounds at the string end; independent Python substring semantics establish empty end/beyond-end intervals and the retained Unicode suffix.
cases.script:
for mode in grapheme codepoint; do
 utf8 slice 'aéx' 3 3 -T "$mode"
 utf8 slice 'aéx' 3 9 -T "$mode"
 utf8 slice 'aéx' 9 9 -T "$mode"
 utf8 slice 'aéx' 1 9 -T "$mode"
done

cases.purpose: Compare short malformed/truncated UTF-8 replacement boundaries directly with independent Python bytes.decode(utf-8,replace), NFC normalization and casefold. These are ordinary encoding inputs; no stress or crash probes.
cases.script:
inputs=( $'\xe2\x82' $'\xf0\x9f\x92' $'\xe2\x82A' $'\xc2B' $'\x80Z' $'\xe0\x80\x80' $'\xed\xa0\x80' $'\xf4\x90\x80\x80' )
for text in "${inputs[@]}"; do
 if [[ $(type -t utf8) == builtin ]]; then
  utf8 length "$text" -T codepoint
  utf8 normalize NFC "$text"
  utf8 casefold "$text"
 else
  printf '%s' "$text" | python3 -c 'import sys,unicodedata; s=sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode("utf-8","replace"); print(len(s)); print(unicodedata.normalize("NFC",s)); print(s.casefold())'
 fi
done

cases.purpose: The same maximal-subpart replacement is used when binding normalized/folded text and comparing after NFC normalization.
cases.script:
bad=$'\xe2\x82'
utf8 normalize NFC "$bad" -V normalized
utf8 casefold "$bad" -V folded
[[ $normalized == $'\xef\xbf\xbd' && $folded == $'\xef\xbf\xbd' ]]
utf8 cmp "$bad" $'\xef\xbf\xbd' -N NFC
printf 'replacement consistent\n'
